Potency versus efficacy

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

Two agonists act at the same receptor in the same tissue. Both achieve an identical maximal response, but drug A requires one tenth the concentration of drug B to produce half of its maximum. Which comparison is correct?

  1. B is more potent with equal efficacy
  2. Potency cannot differ if maxima are equal
  3. A is more potent, with equal maximal efficacy
  4. A is less potent and more efficacious
  5. A is more efficacious but equally potent
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

A is more potent, with equal maximal efficacy

Lower EC50 indicates higher potency, while equal maxima indicate equal efficacy in this system.

Understanding the options

A is more potent, with equal maximal efficacy
Lower EC50 indicates higher potency, while equal maxima indicate equal efficacy in this system.
A is less potent and more efficacious
Both parts conflict with the observations.
A is more efficacious but equally potent
The maxima are equal while EC50 differs.
B is more potent with equal efficacy
B requires a higher concentration, indicating lower potency.
Potency cannot differ if maxima are equal
Potency and maximal efficacy are distinct.
